# Melinda Cooper (2017) — Family Values: Between Neoliberalism and the New Social Conservatism

**Original:** https://www.zonebooks.org/books/48-family-values-between-neoliberalism-and-the-new-social-conservatism
**Published in:** Zone Books / Near Futures series, 2017.
**Reading grade (2026-10-17):** Original publisher description, table of contents and edition details read; full text not read

## Exact contribution to the commissioned thesis

Cooper argues that an alliance of market liberalism and conservative family values relies on enforced/reconstituted familial responsibility to support economic policy. The chapters identify welfare reform, family wage, inheritance, student debt, sexuality and family obligations. This is a plausible historically situated route whereby the rhetorical exaltation of the family can coexist with shifting survival and care costs onto actual households.

## Alternative explanations and evidence limits

A publisher synopsis is insufficient to support a detailed causal case in any named jurisdiction. Do not equate conservative family rhetoric with a documented commitment to an unreachable racial breeder ideal. Full chapter reading, primary policy records and class/racial stratification are still required.
